title: The World of AI: Medical Models catalogue on Hugging Face Hub
answer: This is a catalogue page from The World of AI. It lists the 1000 most downloaded open medical models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 27 September 2026. Its most useful contribution is a daily index of clinical and imaging models, though the supplied text is mostly metadata and promotional material rather than analysis.

sections.body: The World of AI publishes this page as a catalogue of medical models. It covers the 1000 most downloaded open medical models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date, refreshed daily. The page states it was last verified on 27 September 2026 and that its source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads. Every model links to its own Hub page. The page also says the site searches the full text of every published page, all built from the same database, including state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents itself as a daily catalogue of the 1000 most downloaded open medical models on the Hugging Face Hub. It says each entry carries licence, downloads, and release date, and that the list is refreshed daily. The source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 27 September 2026. The description begins to mention clinical and imaging models but the supplied text cuts off after that phrase. The page also describes The World of AI as an atlas of artificial intelligence, saying it searches the full text of every published page, all built from the same database. That database includes state AI laws, a lawsuit tracker, a glossary, a tools directory, AI companies, a research library, an MCP server registry, compliance frameworks, sources, people, calculators, and weekly digests. The page carries a citation line for the Medical Models page. It also includes promotional material for books by Stephen R. Jordan, including The Operating Discipline for AI Library series, and for a novel called The AI Lawyer, out 17 August 2026. It lists named audit and assessment services, including The AI Business Enablement Audit and The AI Readiness & Performance Assessment. It says every page is rebuilt daily from primary sources and carries the date it was last verified, and that the site is free to read, free to cite, and free to query.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states that the catalogue covers the 1000 most downloaded open medical models on the Hugging Face Hub. It states that the list is refreshed daily and was last verified on 27 September 2026. It states that the source is the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all time downloads, and that every model links to its own Hub page. It states that The AI Lawyer is out 17 August 2026. It gives no individual model names, download totals, licence names, or clinical performance figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in healthcare can use this source as a pointer to a daily list of open medical models on the Hugging Face Hub. The page says the list includes licence, downloads, and release date, which are practical details when assessing whether a model can be used, reused, or tracked over time. It also says the models are sorted by all time downloads, so the list offers a popularity signal rather than a clinical quality signal. The page links each model to its own Hub page, so a reader can move from the catalogue to the model's own record. Because the supplied text is mostly metadata and promotion, the source is best used as an index, not as an evaluation of safety, efficacy, or regulatory status.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Healthcare

sections.body: The supplied text is a landing page with little substance. It does not name any medical model, give any download count, list any licence, or describe any clinical result. Its description of clinical and imaging models is cut off. The page is partly commercial, with books by Stephen R. Jordan, a novel from SRJ Consulting & Services, and named audit and assessment services. It is dated by its last verified line of 27 September 2026 and says it is refreshed daily, but the text itself is a short catalogue description rather than a full article. It relies on the Hugging Face Hub public API and all time downloads, so it does not cover regulatory approval, clinical validation, or deployment guidance.
